blockers.quote: Last line inside the image: the next time you leave home, turn round at the corner
blockers.why: The planned last line is an instruction to the viewer, which makes it a lesson. Check #12 wants one real line inside the last image, not a moral. Arthur would also read it as a teacher's sign-off. It also names the action the picture already shows (the turn and the wave), which brushes against #11.
blockers.fix: Replace it with a line that belongs to the scene, spoken low and warm, for example: "She's still at the door. Of course she is." Then cut to the end card. Keep the corner, the turn and the wave in the picture only.

suggestions.fix: Give the spoken form and an emotion tag, e.g. [curious, hushed] "What if you knew the last time you'd see someone?" Say it as a contraction, not the title's full forms, and put it after the wave so it lands on the picture.

suggestions.quote: what would you do with them?
suggestions.fix: Keep it as a short question answered at once by the figure acting, e.g. "Forty-two mornings. What would you do with them?" followed by a beat of the figure looking up from the phone. Tag it [quiet, curious].

suggestions.quote: you cannot make it endless, you can only make it larger
suggestions.fix: This is the landing line, so it is a complete thought, but it reads like an essay. Contract it and split it: "You can't make it endless. You can make it bigger." Tag it [warm, plain].

suggestions.quote: forty-two, the times you will see her again
suggestions.fix: Add a say.yaml entry so Arthur says "forty-two" in words. Write the spoken line with contractions: "Forty-two. That's how many times you'll see her again." Tag it [hushed, dry].

Digits in the outline are fine, but in the script write "thirty-eight... thirty-seven." Give each number its own take, with a pause and then a flat, quiet read, so the number carries the feeling and the narrator doesn't name it.

suggestions.quote: the counter is a forecast, not a budget
suggestions.fix: Keep the idea but say it as a dry aside, not a definition: "It's not a budget. It's a forecast." Tag it [amused, dry]. Short enough for one breath at 1.1x.
